shots.section: 11 · Thales, 181.23–199.98 (B105–115). Strings and choir climb; breath 187.65–188.55; rest 192.75–193.1.
shots.picture: **The year he named.** Thales looks up. Beside him, in gold incised construction lines (behind him, under the lyric), the payoff sits upper right where the card was. It is a compass arc of twelve new-moon ticks (a year of months, no numbers), closed at each end by a short boundary stroke: Herodotus' οὖρος, "the limit". On "sun" the Sun lights inside the arc, under no particular month; on "dark" the Moon's disk covers it. As dim, unlabelled ornament only: the triangle in a semicircle (upper left) and the shadow stick (lower right), things later writers credited him with. There is no 1/720, no saros, no card and no code: nothing claims a method (production/research/THALES_METHOD.md). 4:5 shows the year arc alone.
shots.text: CARVED `FORETOLD THE SUN WOULD GO DARK` · PLAQUE 184.51 `HE NAMED ONLY THE YEAR` · `HERODOTUS 1.74`

She types on the ticks; on `dt.shift` she leans toward the side monitor as the ΔT map's totality band slides north onto the Halys; the terminal scrolls one line per tick. Cut on the chord to S79.

shots.picture: **Back in-universe: the kings make peace** (v2). On the final stark chord Alyattes of Lydia (left) and Cyaxares of Media (right) seal the oath with the right-hand clasp and one firm shake; each bare forearm carries one thin fresh cut. Herodotus 1.74: these nations "make sworn compacts as do the Greeks; and besides, when they cut the skin of their arms, they lick each other's blood" (no licking, no gore). The mediators, Syennesis of Cilicia and Labynetus of Babylon, watch from the edges in shadow. Dusk by the river after the eclipse; one Caravaggio pool on the clasp; held through the frozen chord, then a hard cut to her grin. A small plaque, `THE OATH · HERODOTUS 1.74`, sits lower left from 270.45 (drawn by the scene with the plaque renderer, so it is not a track cue).
